This page continues from steps 2 and 3 and uses their objects `wx`, `traj`, `drv`, `Theta` and `tr`. To start here, load them as described on the [Set up](setup.html) page.


For one genotype, the data are the growth rates $\frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt}$ and the library values $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ of step 3, and the unknown is the coefficient vector $\boldsymbol{\xi}$:

$$
\frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} \approx \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi}.
$$

Every method maps $(\boldsymbol{\Theta}, \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt})$ to an estimate $\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}$, with the intercept first. A method is therefore a function `fit(Theta, dy)`, and methods can be exchanged freely. Genotype `g001` is used here.

## Methods

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Least squares

The reference: all terms are used, so there is no sparsity.

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \; \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2
$$

Hyperparameters: none.

R: `lm.fit`. Python: `numpy.linalg.lstsq`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_ols", level = 3)
```

## Ridge

Shrinks the coefficients towards zero. Correlated terms share their weight, but none is removed.

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \; \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 + \lambda \lVert \boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $\lambda$: strength of the penalty; shrinks the coefficients of correlated terms, but removes none.

Closed form, with the penalty scaled as in `glmnet`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_ridge", level = 3)
```

## Lasso

The $\ell_1$ penalty sets coefficients exactly to zero, which gives a sparse equation.

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \; \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 + \lambda \lVert \boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_1
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $\lambda$: strength of the penalty; larger values set more coefficients to zero.

R: `glmnet`. Python: scikit-learn `ElasticNet`, with the penalty scaled as in `glmnet`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_glmnet", "fit_lasso", level = 3)
```

## Elastic net

A mix of ridge and lasso: sparse like the lasso, but more stable for correlated terms.

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \; \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 + \lambda \Bigl( \tfrac{1 - \alpha}{2} \lVert \boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 + \alpha \lVert \boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_1 \Bigr)
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $\lambda$: strength of the penalty.
- $\alpha$: mix of the two penalties (here 0.5); keeps groups of correlated terms together more readily than the lasso.

Implementation as for the lasso.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_glmnet", "fit_enet", level = 3)
```

## Best subset

The best model with exactly $k$ terms, found by searching all subsets.

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}} = \arg\min_{\lVert \boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_0 \le k} \; \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2
$$

Algorithm:

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\textbf{for each } S \subset \{1, \dots, K\} \textbf{ with } |S| = k: & \\[2pt]
\quad \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_S \leftarrow \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}_S\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 & \text{least squares on the terms in } S \\[2pt]
\quad \mathrm{RSS}(S) \leftarrow \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}_S\hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_S \rVert_2^2 & \\[2pt]
\textbf{return } \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_{S^*} \text{ with } S^* = \arg\min_S \mathrm{RSS}(S) & \text{coefficients outside } S^* \text{ are zero}
\end{array}
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $k$: number of terms that are kept.

R: `leaps`, which searches all subsets efficiently. Python: computed from the Gram matrix; with $K = 24$ terms the exhaustive search takes about a second per fit, so it is left out of the comparison below.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_subset", level = 3)
```

## Backward elimination

A greedy alternative to best subset: start with all terms and repeatedly remove the one that increases the residual error least.

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
S \leftarrow \{1, \dots, K\} & \text{start with all terms} \\[2pt]
\textbf{while } |S| > k: & \\[2pt]
\quad \Delta_j \leftarrow \mathrm{RSS}(S \setminus \{j\}) - \mathrm{RSS}(S) \quad \text{for each } j \in S & \text{increase of the error without term } j \\[2pt]
\quad S \leftarrow S \setminus \{j^*\}, \quad j^* = \arg\min_{j \in S} \Delta_j & \text{remove the least useful term} \\[2pt]
\textbf{return } \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_S & \text{least squares on } S
\end{array}
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $k$: number of terms that are kept; terms are removed one at a time, starting from all $K$ terms, until $k$ remain.

The same function as best subset, called with `method = "backward"`; the cost grows only polynomially with the number of terms.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_subset", level = 3)
```

## STLSQ

Sequential thresholded least squares, the algorithm of the original SINDy method.

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
S \leftarrow \{1, \dots, K\} & \text{start with all terms} \\[2pt]
\textbf{repeat:} & \\[2pt]
\quad \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_S \leftarrow \arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \lVert \frac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt} - \boldsymbol{\Theta}_S\boldsymbol{\xi} \rVert_2^2 & \text{least squares on the active terms} \\[2pt]
\quad S' \leftarrow \bigl\{ j \in S : |\hat{\xi}_j|\, s_j \ge \tau \bigr\}, \quad s_j = \mathrm{sd}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}_j) / \mathrm{sd}\bigl(\tfrac{d\mathbf{y}}{dt}\bigr) & \text{keep the terms above the threshold} \\[2pt]
\quad \textbf{if } S' = S \text{ or } S' = \emptyset \textbf{ then stop, else } S \leftarrow S' & \\[2pt]
\textbf{return } \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}_S & \text{coefficients outside } S \text{ are zero}
\end{array}
$$

Hyperparameters:

- $\tau$: threshold on the scaled coefficient $|\hat{\xi}_j|\,s_j$.

Least squares on the active set $S$, so there is no shrinkage.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_stlsq", level = 3)
```

## Python

```python
size = d.Theta.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / d.dy.std(ddof=1)
effect = fits.iloc[1:].mul(size, axis=0)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(effect.shape[1], 1, sharex=True, sharey=True,
                         figsize=(6.2, 6.2))
for ax, (name, column) in zip(axes, effect.items()):
    ax.bar(column.index, column, color=np.where(column > 0, BLUE, BURGUNDY))
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=8, loc="left")
axes[-1].tick_params(axis="x", rotation=90)
fig.supylabel("scaled coefficient")
fig.tight_layout()
```

```{r}
#| label: 04-3-run

size <- apply(d$Theta, 2, sd) / sd(d$dy)
effect <- fits[-1, ] * size
long <- data.frame(term = factor(rownames(effect), rownames(effect)),
                   method = factor(rep(colnames(effect), each = nrow(effect)),
                                   colnames(effect)),
                   effect = as.vector(effect))
long <- long[long$effect != 0, ]

ggplot(long, aes(term, effect, fill = effect > 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = dgxe[["blue"]],
                               `FALSE` = dgxe[["burgundy"]]),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "scaled coefficient") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7, angle = 90, hjust = 1,
                                   vjust = 0.5))
```

:::

The coefficients of correlated terms are not determined individually (powers of one driver, and thermal time and day length, are strongly correlated), so the selected terms differ between methods. The methods are compared by prediction on unseen years in step 5.

## Exploring a method

Each method has one hyperparameter. Switch genotypes on and off to compare their coefficients (top); the lower panel shows the held-out error for all settings, as the mean over 20 genotypes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = window.d3
Plot = window.Plot
hyper = FileAttachment("data/interactive/hyper.json").json()
contrast = ["g181", "g171", "g021", "g141", "g151"]
shades = ["#8B1E3F", "#014E81", "#00A6D6", "#6D8B1E", "#6B7280"]
viewof method = select("Method", Object.keys(hyper.methods), "STLSQ")
spec = hyper.methods[method]
viewof shown = toggles("Genotypes", contrast, shades)
viewof step = slider(spec.param, spec.values, Math.floor(spec.values.length / 2), v => (+v).toPrecision(2))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const all = Object.values(hyper.methods);
  const reach = d3.max(all.flatMap(m => m.effect.flat(2).map(Math.abs)));
  const rmse = [d3.min(all.flatMap(m => m.rmse)), 0.8];   // cap: very large penalties are off scale
  const band = 5, n = shown.length;
  const key = (term, name) => term + "|" + name;
  const domain = hyper.terms.flatMap(term => [...shown.map(name => key(term, name)), key(term, "")]);
  const middle = hyper.terms.map(term => key(term, shown[Math.floor(n / 2)]));
  const rows = shown.flatMap(name => {
    const g = hyper.genotypes.indexOf(name);
    return hyper.terms.map((term, i) => ({name, band: key(term, name), effect: spec.effect[step][g][i]}));
  });
  const coefficients = Plot.plot({
    width: 56 + band * domain.length, height: 250, marginLeft: 56, marginBottom: 60,
    y: {domain: [-reach, reach], label: "scaled coefficient", ticks: 4},
    x: {domain, ticks: middle, tickFormat: d => d.split("|")[0], tickRotate: -90, label: null, padding: 0},
    color: {domain: contrast, range: shades},
    marks: [Plot.barY(rows, {x: "band", y: "effect", fill: "name"}), Plot.ruleY([0])]
  });
  const curve = spec.values.map((value, i) => ({value, rmse: spec.rmse[i]}));
  const scale = spec.param === "terms" ? "linear" : "log";
  const error = Plot.plot({
    width: 520, height: 220,
    x: {type: scale, label: spec.param, tickFormat: ".2~g"},
    y: {domain: [rmse[0] - 0.01, rmse[1] + 0.01], label: "held-out RMSE (t/ha)"},
    marks: [Plot.line(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", stroke: "#9CA3AF", clip: true}),
            Plot.dot(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#9CA3AF", r: 3, clip: true}),
            Plot.dot([curve[step]], {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#8B1E3F", r: 6, clip: true})]
  });
  return html`<div><div class="scroll-x">${coefficients}</div>${error}</div>`;
}
```
